parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: $(2\ln a+\ln b)y=(\ln b)x+\ln a$, which is linear in $x$ and $y$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Use logarithms to obtain a correct expression without powers, e.g. $(2y-1)\ln a=(x-y)\ln b$; logs to any base are allowed and missing brackets are not condoned unless recovered. [B1] Separate terms and factorise to obtain $(2\ln a+\ln b)y=x\ln b+\ln a$, or equivalent. [B1] Give a clear explanation that the correct equation matches $y=mx+c$ or $py=qx+r$; merely calling it linear without comparison to a standard form scores B0. [B1] Total: 3.

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Use $a=b^3$ and logarithm laws to simplify the equation from part (a), with the denominator reduced to a single logarithm term. [M1] Obtain $y=\frac17x+\frac37$; accept $7y=x+3$ but not an ambiguous unsimplified form. [A1] Alternative: substitute $a=b^3$ directly into the original exponential equation [M1] and obtain the same line [A1]. Total: 2.
